transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-21
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Ravi Menon (CTO - Alder Labs), Elena Sosa (Senior Platform Engineer - Alder), Markus Hahn (NetOps - Alder)

Summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on recent kernel/quantization upgrade impact, egress shaping, telemetry gaps, and rollout gating for canary. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share changelog and canary playbook; Alder to provide egress/firewall configs and enable sFlow; schedule burn test on canary.

[00:00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining for the weekly P O C sync, we got a packed agenda today, small housekeeping, i'll run through notes, maya will cover the kernel/quant results, and then we'll triage the remaining egress telemetry gaps.
[00:00:18] Ravi: yep sounds good, we're on a slightly different timezone today so apologies if i drop a bit early, but hopefully we get the canary plan sorted.
[00:00:26] Maya: okay cool i'll jump in with the perf summary. quick note, the last kernel build we pushed to the private canary pool had two changes: one was the new attention kernel fallback, and second was quant path adjustments for int8 mixed mode. the build id is rn-2027-07-k14, see the short notes link (doc: https://redwood.company/pilot/changelogs/rn-2027-07-k14)
[00:00:52] Elena: i got the link, thanks. quick question — we observed a handful of 5xx spikes last night; any idea if those were related to the kernel swap?
[00:01:02] Maya: good call. we traced most of those to a connection reset between the edge nat gateway and the canary nodes; there was a subtle socket backlog change in the new kernel that, under our current egress shaping, hit worker queues and caused retries. not absolute 5xx from model, more infra-level resets and our retry logic bubbled it up.
[00:01:24] Markus: when you say "egress shaping", do you mean the token egress traffic shaping you mentioned before or our customer NAT rate limits? we have a per-conn limit on the NAT gateway and then a broadband firewall policy at the cloud edge.
[00:01:37] Jordan: both actually, in practice they interact. the platform's internal burst control + your NAT timeout/rate caps led to increased TCP retries. so small bursts that used to be absorbed are now hitting your nat and getting reset.
[00:01:50] Ravi: ok that matches what we saw; flow logs show many short-lived tcp connects to redwood nodes at 16:30 UTC, then resets. we also have a couple of deny rules that might be throttling return traffic.
[00:02:03] Maya: next step there is we want the egress ACLs and NAT config to confirm. on the Redwood side we can adjust the socket backlog and reduce retry windows for the canary pool so we don't cascade into 5xx for user requests.
[00:02:15] Elena: we'll pull the NAT config but i also want to make sure this won't surface at scale. what's your recommended rollback window if we see p95/p99 regressions?
[00:02:25] Jordan: good question. our canary playbook has an automatic 15 minute hold if p99 increases by more than 30% and error rate crosses 0.5% for 5 consecutive minutes, with an immediate rollback option from the console. we'll share the formal playbook.
[00:02:40] Maya: adding to that, we also instrument a KV cache warmup so cold starts don't hit the model at the same time. the last run showed 8% faster median token latencies after warmup, but tail still had occasional spikes tied to egress resets.
[00:02:58] [00:03:05] Markus: hmm warmup is interesting — can we push warmup connections through a different subnet to avoid NAT limits? we have spare private subnet ips we can dedicate.
[00:03:15] Maya: yes that's feasible, we can route warmups through a separate egress path. that would avoid ratelimiting collision with live traffic. it'd need a short network config change on your side or a proxy in front.
[00:03:28] Ravi: let's add that as an action. Markus you'll own exposing the spare subnet?
[00:03:33] Markus: yep i'll take that.
[00:03:36] Jordan: perfect. ok next major topic — telemetry. we got the telemetry bundle from your devops but there are still gaps in flow logs around the edge routers between 03:00 and 03:45 UTC; missing spans make it hard to correlate tail latency with upstream retries.
[00:03:52] Elena: correct, we had a short flow-collector outage overnight and some logs were lost. we can re-enable sFlow and push historical exports to the telemetry bucket, but we need an access ticket for the S3 bucket.
[00:04:05] Maya: if you can enable sFlow and give us read only to telemetry-redwood-alder, we can overlay traces with token-level timing. that was the key ask from product for defect triage.
[00:04:16] Elena: i'll create the ticket post call.
[00:04:20] [00:04:30] Jordan: excellent. i want to call out an observed mismatch in our sampling config — the Redwood agent uses adaptive sampling that samples at higher rates when we detect retry loops. your netflow sampler is at fixed 1% which misses these short bursts.
[00:04:46] Markus: oh, that's probably why. we can bump to 5% but that increases cost in the telemetry bucket. what's the minimum you need to be useful?
[00:04:56] Maya: 2.5% with burst windowing for the 10 minute canary window is usually actionable. we can do a temporary bump for the canary tests.
[00:05:08] Ravi: okay let's do that for the next run.
[00:05:11] Jordan: moving on, we did some regression testing against the p99 SLA for 1k rps baseline. summary: median and p95 held within expected ranges, p99 increased by ~22% for certain long prompts when quant path was used. the quant path improvement for cost is material but we need to tune prompts that trigger long KV cache chains.
[00:05:34] Maya: yeah the int8 mixed path reduces token compute by roughly 40% on average, but for sequences with large KV reuse the decode path flips to a slower fallback for correctness in a few ops — that's what's spiking the tail. we can change the threshold for falling back to the safe path.
[00:05:52] Elena: are those thresholds configurable from the console or do you need to recompile per farm?
[00:05:57] Maya: currently it's a config flag that we can flip per-pool; no recompile. we'll provide the recommended values and safe rollback.
[00:06:06] [00:06:15] Markus: i want to surface one more networking oddity — during a midday test we saw asymmetric routing where responses returned via a different NAT and hit a stricter firewall rule. could that be a cause for the retries?
[00:06:26] Jordan: yes that can cause unexpected resets. our client side retries don't anticipate different egress IPs; they'll retrigger but if the firewall treats the new egress as unknown it may drop sessions. so we need the NAT sticky mapping or ensure firewall allows both candidate IPs.
[00:06:40] Ravi: we can check the sticky NAT settings. Markus will follow up with the cloud provider on preserving 5-tuple mapping.
[00:06:48] Markus: noted.
[00:06:51] Maya: for the canary we recommend a conservative approach: 1) increase telemetry sampling to 2.5% during burn; 2) route warmup through dedicated subnet; 3) temporarily relax NAT per-conn limits to accommodate warmup bursts; 4) Redwood flips kernel backlog and retry windows to minimize retries. if those are in place we expect the p99 delta to shrink to under 10%.
[00:07:18] Elena: sounds good. how long is the burn window you want?
[00:07:22] Jordan: we typically do a 2-hour burn to capture diurnal patterns, with synthetic traffic at different prompt shapes. and we recommend a second run during a higher utilization period to test tail.
[00:07:33] Ravi: schedule it next week, week of 2027-07-26. i've blocked windows; we'll confirm the exact 2-hour slot.
[00:07:40] [00:07:50] Jordan: action item — jordan to send the explicit canary playbook and rollback thresholds. maya will attach the microbench and p95/p99 baseline sheets.
[00:07:58] Maya: yep i'll include the quant threshold knobs and the recommended values per workload.
[00:08:04] Markus: one quick legal/compliance note — if we increase telemetry sampling there are PII considerations. we need to ensure token-level traces are redacted before they land in our telemetry storage.
[00:08:16] Jordan: absolutely, we will filter sensitive fields at source and only ingest meta/timing. i'll include the data retention and redaction snippets in the playbook.
[00:08:26] Elena: thanks. also two items from our side — we want a short runbook for on-call to follow if the canary triggers rollback, and a checklist for switching back to stable nodes.
[00:08:36] Maya: we'll share a concise on-call checklist with explicit console steps and the single-button rollback.
[00:08:43] [00:08:50] Ravi: moving to commercial, the pricing band for the dedicated canary pool we discussed last week — any change after the quantization adjustments?
[00:08:59] Jordan: the cost per token goes down with the int8 path but because of potential tail overhead we recommend we keep current trial pricing until we validate the burn results. we can then adjust and reflect the savings.
[00:09:12] Ravi: fair enough.
[00:09:15] Maya: final technical note: we saw one odd error in the agent logs where a device reported "KV cash missing" — speech-to-text turned it into "kv cache" but the log actually says kv-cache-timeout. it's a config timeout we can safely increase.
[00:09:29] Elena: we will allow a temporary increase to kv-cache timeout for the canary.
[00:09:34] Jordan: great. wrapping up — recap of next steps and owners. Jordan will share the playbook and changelog; Maya will run and attach synthetic results; Elena/Markus will provide egress/firewall configs and enable sFlow; Alder to confirm NAT stickiness and provide flow logs for the last 48 hours.
[00:09:55] Ravi: and we'll confirm the 2-hour burn window next week. thanks all.
[00:10:03] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up by email with the artifacts and a calendar invite for the burn slot.
[00:10:08] [00:10:15] End of meeting notes.

Notes on transcription: occasional misrecognitions (e.g., "kv cash" / "kv cache"; "quantisazion" typed in auto notes), speaker label consistency may vary.
